narek.tagline: Infrastructure for building, orchestrating, and governing enterprise AI agents.
narek.description: A platform for running, orchestrating, and governing AI agents — built for engineering teams that need agent behavior backed by real infrastructure: a runtime, retrieval and memory layers, tool execution, and policy-based governance.

problem.headline: Building an AI agent is easy. Operating one is not.
problem.description: Runtime orchestration, retrieval, prompt versioning, tool execution, conversation memory, access control, and execution traceability are all required before an agent can be trusted with a real workload. Most teams end up building fragile, one-off versions of each, tied to a single project and a single model provider.

capabilities.title: Agent Runtime & Orchestration
capabilities.description: Executes AI agents and coordinates their workflows end to end — with retrieval, memory, tool access, and policy enforcement built into the execution layer.

capabilities.title: RAG & Knowledge Management
capabilities.description: Document ingestion and vector search over PostgreSQL + pgvector to ground agent responses in retrieved knowledge. Agents retrieve from an organized knowledge base, not raw files.

capabilities.title: Execution Traceability
capabilities.description: Every agent run is recorded end to end — from retrieval to response — for audit and debugging. Full traces, logs, and metrics for every execution.

insight.message: "Configure an agent, trigger it, inspect the result."
insight.evidence: The platform abstracts agent execution behind a runtime that handles retrieval, memory, tool access, and policy enforcement. Each run is fully traceable — the user configures an agent from the dashboard, triggers it, and inspects the complete execution trace afterward.

philosophy.headline: Build AI agents, not chatbots.
philosophy.description: Narek provides the infrastructure layer underneath AI applications: agent execution, knowledge retrieval, prompt management, memory, tool access, and governance — so teams can build applications on top without reimplementing them for every project.

pillars.label: Provider-agnostic
pillars.description: No hard dependency on a single model vendor — Spring AI decouples agent logic from the LLM backend.

pillars.label: Governed
pillars.description: Access control and observability are part of the platform, not an afterthought.

pillars.label: Modular
pillars.description: Runtime, memory, retrieval, and tools are separable services, not a monolith.

decisions.title: Agent-first architecture
decisions.description: Built to run and govern agents as first-class units, not to wrap a single conversational assistant.
decisions.why: Enterprise AI needs orchestration, governance, and traceability — not just a chat interface.

decisions.title: Provider abstraction
decisions.description: Agent logic sits behind Spring AI's model abstraction, not a specific vendor SDK, so the LLM backend can change without touching agent code.
decisions.why: No vendor lock-in — agents run on Ollama locally today, with OpenRouter planned for multi-provider access.

decisions.title: Governance built in
decisions.description: A dedicated policy engine controls agent access and actions, instead of relying on prompt-level rules.
decisions.why: Policy enforcement belongs in the infrastructure, not in the prompt.

decisions.title: Full execution traceability
decisions.description: Every agent run is recorded end to end, from retrieval to response, for audit and debugging.
decisions.why: When an agent makes a decision, you need to know exactly how it got there.

narek.decisionsScreenshotCaption: Execution trace — full agent run recorded from retrieval to response, with timing and step details

architecture.detail: The Angular dashboard talks to a Spring Boot API, which fans out to three core services: the Agent Runtime, the Policy Engine, and the Model Router. The Agent Runtime coordinates execution and delegates to the Memory Service and Tool Registry; the Knowledge Service handles retrieval against a pgvector-backed vector store. The Model Router dispatches requests to the configured AI Provider — Ollama for local execution today, with OpenRouter planned for multi-provider access.

narek.status: Core stack is built: Spring Boot, Spring AI, Ollama, Angular dashboard, agent runtime, RAG with pgvector, memory, and observability basics. Currently building the policy engine, tool registry, and workflow engine.

subtextai.description: An AI engine that analyzes conversations to surface intent, emotional shifts, and hidden meaning with every interpretation grounded in evidence, scored with calibrated confidence, and fully traceable.

problem.headline: Conversations are easy to misread.
problem.description: The problem isn't what someone says it's what they might actually mean. Most AI tools answer with the same confidence whether they have real evidence or not. In a domain where the answer shapes personal decisions, that unearned confidence is the problem.

capabilities.title: Conversation Analysis
capabilities.description: Paste any ambiguous message with its context and get a complete pragmatic analysis: overall tone, emotional signals, hidden meaning, key behavioral insights, and a suggested response all grounded in documentary evidence.

capabilities.title: Replay Mode
capabilities.description: Transform any analyzed conversation into an interactive timeline of emotion, intent, and tension like a replay of human decisions. Includes autoplay with a tension heatmap and per-message subtext explanations.

capabilities.title: Live Session Telemetry
capabilities.description: Real-time panel tracking emotional velocity, conflict acceleration, and conversational friction as the conversation unfolds, message by message. Metrics update live as messages are exchanged.

insight.evidence: The phrase "whatever" combined with the curt phrasing signals emotional withdrawal. The use of minimal agreement ("if you want") without enthusiasm indicates frustration rather than genuine consent. Linguistic markers suggest the speaker feels unheard.

philosophy.headline: AI shouldn't be a black box.
philosophy.description: SubtextAI is designed so that every interpretation is defensible. The system doesn't just generate answers it explains why, shows its sources, and knows when to stay silent.

pillars.label: Grounded
pillars.description: Every interpretation backed by retrieved documentary evidence.

pillars.label: Scored
pillars.description: Confidence calculated objectively by a cross-encoder, not assumed.

pillars.label: Traceable
pillars.description: Every response reconstructible by trace_id — documents, scores, model, prompt version.

decisions.title: Evidence before generation
decisions.description: The model never generates unless relevant documents were retrieved first. No evidence, no response.
decisions.why: In a domain where answers shape personal decisions, ungrounded confidence is worse than no answer.

decisions.title: Confidence as a gate
decisions.description: A cross-encoder reranker scores retrieved evidence. If the score falls below a calibrated threshold, generation is blocked entirely.
decisions.why: The system knows when it doesn't know — and says so instead of guessing.

decisions.title: Traceable responses
decisions.description: Every response carries a trace_id linking to the retrieved documents, reranker scores, prompt version, model used, and policies evaluated.
decisions.why: Full auditability — any interpretation can be reconstructed and verified after the fact.

decisions.title: Privacy by design
decisions.description: Raw conversation text and audit annotations are stored in separate data stores, so erasure requests and retention limits never break the audit trail.

architecture.detail: FastAPI orchestrates the pipeline with LangGraph. Policy validation and crisis classification run first (crisis detection is blocking but parallel to retrieval). Hybrid search combines pgvector HNSW cosine similarity with tsvector/GIN lexical search, fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion. A cross-encoder reranker acts as the confidence gate — if no retrieved fragment scores above the calibrated threshold, generation is blocked. Inference runs through OpenRouter (GPT-4.1 for analysis, text-embedding-3-large for embeddings). The full stack deploys on a single AWS EC2 t3.micro instance via Docker Compose (FastAPI + PostgreSQL/pgvector + Redis + Nginx), with Amplify Hosting for the frontend and Secrets Manager for the single external credential.

subtextai.status: Architecture and product design are done. Right now I'm building the backend: policy engine, retrieval, reranking, and traceability — targeting a production AWS deployment.
